messages:
alex: quick sync — onboarding orion-mini-int4 on dedicated canary uncovered a weird class of structured-output parse failures. fp16 baseline parse_fail ~0.7%, orion-mini-int4 = 4.1%
alex: failure pattern: streaming/chunked outputs that include multibyte characters (accented names, emojis) sometimes get split across chunk boundaries and produce invalid UTF-8 or broken escape sequences for downstream JSON parser
ravi: sample frames (captured from a failing stream):
```
frame1: {\"action\":\"create_user\",\"name\":\"Zo
frame2: \"ë\",\"bio\":\"Loves ☕️ and C++\"}
```
ravi: naive concat yields the right string in many cases but some client parsers validate UTF-8 per-frame and error early: "invalid byte sequence" or JSON parse error at offset X
mei: hypothesis: quantized tokenizers + int4 flush policy can cut token byte sequences mid-codepoint more often. token-boundary grid shifts slightly after quantization which increases mid-codepoint splits when chunking by token count
infra-bot: Canary report: model=orion-mini-int4 total=6000 pass=95.9% parse_fail=4.1% delta=+3.4% vs baseline
mei: quick diagnostics we can run: (1) replay with codepoint-aware chunking at runtime, (2) replay with ascii-escape mode (escape non-ascii to \uXXXX) and measure parse_fail, (3) collect tokenization->byte-offset histograms for fp16 vs int4
alex: I ran a 1k replay with ascii-escape preprocessor (server escapes non-ascii before streaming). parse_fail dropped to 0.9% — promising but it's a behavioral change for clients if unescaped payloads expected
ravi: alternatives: (A) base64-envelope: emit payload as base64 string in one token-safe chunk so client decodes after full assemble, (B) enforce chunk flush at codepoint boundaries in runtime, (C) client-side tolerant re-decoder that joins adjacent frames and retries decode before failing
mei: runtime fix (flush-at-codepoint) is ideal but touches kernel/emit path; will need a patch and perf regression checks. base64 shim is fast to roll out for canary only
alex: short-term mitigations proposed: 1) enable base64_canary=true for orion-mini-int4 streaming canary (server emits base64 payloads), 2) bump funcall retry budget 2->4 for int4 variant, 3) client libs: add join-and-try-decode fallback before marking parse fail
infra-bot: Actionable tasks created: TASK-ML-421: gather token-byte-offset histograms (owner=mei), TASK-OPS-882: implement base64_canary flag & metric (owner=ravi), TASK-SDK-77: add streaming-decode-fallback in SDKs (owner=alex)
mei: also recommend adding a small parser lint in postprocess: if UTF-8 decode fails, attempt to reassemble last N frames and use "utf-8-sanitize" routine that replaces lone continuation bytes with replacement char \uFFFD and then run JSON-repair heuristics
ravi: note: ensure idempotency headers survive retries if we increase retry budget. we've seen duplicate-toolcall issues when retries generate new ids (we should use stable X-client-funcall-id)
alex: agree. we'll wire stable header in the canary SDK flag as part of TASK-SDK-77. also collect 10 full raw fails for offline analysis and attach to TASK-ML-421
infra-bot: Canary run scheduled: 10k samples with base64_canary=true starting 1780007200 UTC
alex: thanks team. tagging @mei @ravi to coordinate. will update canary playbook and dashboard tile for parse_fail_by_unicode_presence. :thumbsup:
